description:
***  Viewings from Saturday 5th September. ***

This 1950`s end of terrace family home is situated on a generous end terrace plot in the scenic semi rural location that is Batheaston to the east of Bath. 

Being end of terrace, the combined front and side gardens offer plenty of space with two forms of entry to both the main entrance hallway and the dining room set back to the side garden.

The heart of the home is a bright, dual aspect sitting room centred around a working open fireplace with large windows to the front and rear maximising natural daylight. A modern, well appointed kitchen flows effortlessly into a separate dining room, which benefits from its own external access doors to both the rear and front gardens creating a highly functional layout for both family living and entertaining. A guest WC positioned off the entrance hall completes the ground floor accommodation. Upstairs, a generous first floor landing connects the rest of the home. There are three well proportioned bedrooms, each positioned to take advantage of scenic views over the surrounding countryside and a modern family shower room completes the first floor.

Externally, the superb terraced rear garden has been landscaped to include a full width patio seating terrace accessed from the dining room with an extensive lawn leading up to an upper patio terrace positioned to the rear left hand boundary to make the most of the views and to catch the late day sun. 

Catherine Way lies on the edge of Batheaston approximately 3 miles to the east of Bath. The properties here were built in the 1950s and the area is a popular location for families to enjoy the semi-rural views, the excellent amenities Batheaston village has to offer and the excellent local primary school. This is a great area to live with excellent walks to the top of Solsbury Hill offering spectacular views. The local school at Batheaston is highly praised with a pedestrian route from Catherine Way making it a pleasant school run in the mornings. You can access the Limestone Link walk that connects the Cotswolds to the Mendips with the pretty village of St Catherine along the route. Commuters are on the right side of Bath for an easy access to the motorway without having to cross the city.
